sources.entry: Owncast - Decentralized single-user live video streaming and chat server for running your own live streams similar in style to the large mainstream options. (Source Code) MIT Go
Owncast | Self-hosted live video streaming and chat server

summary.one_liner: Owncast is a self-hosted, single-user live video streaming and chat server that lets you run your own live streams, accepting broadcasts over RTMP.
summary.what_it_does: Owncast is an open source server for running your own live video streams with a built-in chat. The README says it works with any broadcasting software that sends RTMP to a remote server, and names OBS, Streamlabs and Restream as tools that have been used with it. The backend is written in Go and the web frontend (player, chat, embed components) is written in React. The README says the goal is a single service that works out of the box, with a Quickstart in the docs. It also describes complete ownership over content, interface, moderation and audience. The README does not detail specific features beyond these.
use_cases: run my own livestream with chat
stream from OBS to my own server
embed a live stream player on a website
how_to_run: Install prerequisites: a C compiler (GCC or Musl-compatible) and ffmpeg
Install the Go toolchain (1.24 or above)
Run `go run main.go` from the backend source
Visit the web interface or admin address shown in the output
Point your broadcasting software (RTMP) at the new server and start streaming
For the frontend: in the `web` directory run `npm install` then `npm run dev`
notable: Single-service design intended to work out of the box, with a Quickstart guide
Compatible with any RTMP-based broadcasting software, such as OBS
Backend in Go, web interface and player in React
Branch and tag model: develop is latest, release tags give stable versions
caveats: Does not natively support Windows servers; WSL2 is suggested
Building from source requires Go 1.24+, a C compiler and ffmpeg
The develop branch may be unstable compared with tagged releases
